clue.text: Irritable, son needing diaper

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
nappy is the British word for a diaper

explanation.surface: A cranky child wants a fresh diaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fractious baby, but Irritable is the definition and the rest is building material.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes someone short-tempered who answers sharply, a synonym for irritable.

clue.text: Warning about sailors in house

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a sign can be a warning or omen
tars is an old word for sailors

explanation.surface: A notice warns about sailors inside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: House looks like a building, but in astrology a house is a division of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology the twelve signs of the zodiac are also called houses, so a star sign is a house.

clue.text: Room, a dry one on top of condo

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal, someone who is dry
I is the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of condo

explanation.surface: A dry room sits at the top of a condominium block.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's attic-on-top-of-the-building picture is apt, though each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room just under the roof of a house.

clue.text: Professional salesmen, upwardly mobile, do well

indicators.note: in a down clue moving upwards means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pro is short for professional
reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: Ambitious professional salespeople climb the ladder and thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Upwardly mobile sounds like social climbing, but in a down clue it means the word reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to flourish and succeed, which is what doing well means.

clue.text: Policeman parking behind drug company

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the word before it is placed at the end of the answer

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
CO is the abbreviation for company
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: An officer parks his car behind a pharmaceutical firm's building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the parking letter after the drug and company pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed cop is an informal term for a traffic officer who catches motorists going too fast.

clue.text: One's used to measure wind speed and test swell

definitions.text: One's used to measure wind speed

blocks.note: to pilot a scheme is to trial it
to balloon is to swell up

explanation.surface: A meteorological device gauges wind speed and checks for ocean swell.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell looks like a sea wave fitting the weather picture, but it is a verb meaning expand.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists release a small pilot balloon and track it to find wind speed and direction aloft.

clue.text: Choose artist to portray legendary Greek daughter

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: Someone selects an artist to paint a mythical Greek heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra was the daughter of Agamemnon who avenged his murder.

clue.text: Cautioner misrepresented a liqueur

indicators.note: misrepresented means given a false shape, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone giving a warning gave a false picture of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured spirit, a well-known brand of triple sec.

clue.text: A girl wanting pepper on a rice dish

blocks.note: P, the initial of pepper
taken as written
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wants pepper sprinkled on her rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' joins the girl to the pepper piece, which goes on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish dish of saffron rice cooked with seafood or chicken.

clue.text: One foremost in universe — God the Creator

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: a means one, as in a single thing
the first letter of universe
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A grand statement about the first being of the cosmos, God the Creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God the Creator' reads as one phrase, but God supplies the Norse deity and only Creator is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the originator or maker of something, so creator is a synonym.

clue.text: Dirty duck by English river

blocks.note: blue means smutty or risqué, as in blue jokes
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A grubby duck paddles beside an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck looks like a bird on the riverbank; in cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Nile is the great river flowing from Ethiopia to join the White Nile at Khartoum.

clue.text: Harmonica virtuoso's appearing in stylish south London theatre

indicators.note: appearing in means turning up inside, so one piece is set within another

blocks.note: swell is dated slang for smart or fashionable
Larry Adler was a celebrated harmonica player
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A harmonica star performs at a smart theatre in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South London theatre' reads as one phrase, but south supplies a letter; the theatre is in Islington, north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadler's Wells is a renowned dance theatre in London, home to many ballet and dance companies.

clue.text: Mad psycho confronting social worker, a toady

indicators.note: mad suggests something deranged and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
an ant is a worker insect living in a colony, hence social

explanation.surface: A deranged psycho confronts a social worker, who turns out to be a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker here is not a welfare officer but an insect: ants live in organised colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns on the powerful to win favour, which is exactly what a toady does.

clue.text: Reckon baby has a litre

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Someone estimates that the baby drinks a litre of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To total is to add up a sum, and reckon also means to calculate or count up.

clue.text: A merger — an angle exercising chief executive

indicators.note: exercising puts things through their paces and works them about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company boss is busy working out the best angle on a merger deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The business vocabulary of merger and chief executive makes the clue feel like straight description, but the letters of the first five words rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A general manager runs a company's overall operations, a role close to that of a chief executive.

clue.text: Fruit drink that's delicious in the heart of Guatemala

indicators.note: the heart is the very centre, so only the middle letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: nectar is a delicious drink, the drink of the gods
taken as written
the middle letter of the nine-letter Guatemala

explanation.surface: A tasty fruit drink is found in central Guatemala.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Fish cooked ashore in the south-east

indicators.note: cooked suggests preparing and transforming, so the letters are mixed up
in means inside, so the jumble sits between the compass letters

blocks.note: taken as written
SE is the abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Fish is cooked on the beach in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The seahorse is a small marine fish with a horse-like head that swims upright.

clue.text: Plant in Greece I bet cult destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means smashed to pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wagers that a religious sect in Greece was wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant in Greece' reads like a Mediterranean flower, but Plant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg lettuce is a crisp, pale salad vegetable, and any lettuce is a leafy plant.

clue.text: Huge stroke of luck finding old cowboy series on TV

blocks.note: first meaning: a windfall or source of great wealth
second meaning: the long-running American western about the Cartwright family

explanation.surface: Someone strikes it lucky by stumbling on a classic western series.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a rich vein of ore and so any windfall; it was also the title of the 1959-73 TV western.

clue.text: Walkway that POW rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means constructed again in a new form, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war reconstructed a footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: POW, prisoner of war, suggests labour camps building roads, but here it is just three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A towpath runs alongside a canal or river, a walkway once used by horses towing barges.

clue.text: Constant interference

blocks.note: first meaning: unchanging, not moving
second meaning: crackling noise on a radio or TV

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as a single complaint about persistent meddling; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Static as an adjective means fixed and unchanging; as a noun it is electrical disturbance on a broadcast signal.

clue.text: US writer has drop of American in double

indicators.note: a drop is just a tiny amount, so only one letter, the opening one, is taken
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a twin is a double, an exact match
the first letter of American

explanation.surface: An American author keeps a drop of something American in his double.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain's pen name fits neatly, as twain itself is an old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn, is one of the most famous writers from the United States.

clue.text: Fleece not entirely fit US businessman

indicators.note: not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a fleece is a sheep's coat of wool
fit in the sense of deserving or suitable

explanation.surface: A con man who swindles people is not quite fit to be called a businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleece looks like a verb meaning swindle, which suits a dodgy businessman, but here it is the sheep's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Woolworth was the American retailer who founded the Woolworth chain of five-and-dime stores.

clue.text: Puzzle concerning old car

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
bus is dated slang for a car

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a vintage motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a word puzzle in which pictures and symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Musical instrument a girl, ten, ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a sequence, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old girl is told to take up a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordered sounds like the girl was commanded to play, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into three sides and struck with a beater.

clue.text: Locksmith?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tradesman who makes and repairs door locks
setter's reading: someone who works on locks of hair

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: the locks are tresses rather than door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's hairdresser cuts and styles hair, and locks are tresses of hair, so he is a craftsman of locks.

clue.text: Folding creases seen round very deep fissure

indicators.note: folding bends and rearranges material, so the letters are refolded into a new order
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Folded creases in fabric look like a very deep crack.
explanation.walkthrough: The folding creases picture fits the definition so well that the anagram signal is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep open crack, especially in a glacier, so it is a deep fissure.

clue.text: Decent high teas served after church

indicators.note: served suggests dishing something up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A respectable high tea is served after the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the church letters first and the rearranged teas behind them; high is padding for the surface image of high tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means modest and pure in conduct, close in sense to decent.
